entries.clue: Teased terribly for being staid (6)

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

annotation.surface: Someone mocked cruelly just for being a bit dull and proper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teased' looks like the verb of the story, but it is only the raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe someone calm, sober and unadventurous.

entries.clue: Notice servant making gradual escape (7)

blocks.note: to notice = to see
a page is a young servant or attendant

annotation.surface: A servant is spotted slipping quietly away from the household.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'escape' sounds like a runaway servant; it is really liquid slowly leaking out.
annotation.definitionFit: Liquid oozing slowly through a crack or porous wall is escaping gradually.

entries.clue: Take car through flooded river? (5)

indicators.note: the answer runs through the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first four of the second

annotation.surface: A motorist wonders about pushing on through a river in flood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Through' reads as the car's route across the water; it is the signal that the letters run through 'flooded river'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking a car somewhere, at the wheel, is the verb.

entries.clue: Holidaymaker is one having minor accident maybe (7)

blocks.note: British word for someone on a day's outing or excursion
a stumble is one kind of minor accident, and this is the person who stumbles

annotation.surface: A tourist who keeps having little mishaps on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: TRIPPER is a British word for a day-tripper, often a slightly disparaging one; 'maybe' signals that a trip is just one kind of minor accident.
annotation.definitionFit: A British regional use for an excursionist, plus the literal sense of someone who stumbles.

entries.clue: Fellow about to protect chum from inflammatory liquid (6)

indicators.note: about means turned round, so MAN reads backwards
the reversed fellow protects the chum by surrounding it

blocks.note: a fellow is a MAN, turned about
chum = pal

annotation.surface: A man shields his friend from some burning liquid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inflammatory' usually means provocative, as in a speech; here it is literal, something that sets fire.
annotation.definitionFit: It is jellied petrol used in firebombs, so an inflammatory liquid in the most literal sense.

entries.clue: Eastender’s bald and stuffy (7)

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End traditionally drops the H at the start of words

blocks.note: bald = HAIRLESS, said by a Cockney without its H

annotation.surface: A Londoner is described as having no hair and being a bit pompous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuffy' reads as a character trait, stiff and pompous, but it means lacking fresh air. An Eastender is a Londoner from the East End, whose accent drops H.
annotation.definitionFit: A stuffy room is one short of fresh air, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Philosopher ill-disposed to realist (9)

indicators.note: read as badly arranged: the letters are disposed in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

annotation.surface: An idealist thinker who is hostile to realists.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ill-disposed to' reads as unfriendly towards; split it as ill-disposed (badly arranged) acting on 'to realist'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Greek thinker who studied under Plato.

entries.clue: Collection of English language held by this writer (7)

indicators.note: the English language sits inside, held by ME

blocks.note: this writer = the setter, me
E = English
the standard abbreviation for language

annotation.surface: A writer owns a collection of works in English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Collection of English language' reads as one phrase, like an anthology, but 'Collection' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A mixture or assortment, borrowed from French, which is a collection of varied things.

entries.clue: Require theologian to conceal flipping identity! (6)

indicators.note: the theologian hides the name by wrapping round it
to flip something is to turn it over, so the word for identity is read backwards

blocks.note: Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
identity = NAME, flipped

annotation.surface: A theologian is ordered to keep his identity secret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like an exclamation of annoyance, which the '!' encourages; it is the instruction to turn the name over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to insist on something as necessary.

entries.clue: The thing – no doubt about it! (8,7)

blocks.note: the italics mark this as a word under discussion: its grammatical label
a thing (article) that is certain (definite)

annotation.surface: Someone insists that a particular thing is beyond doubt.
annotation.walkthrough: The italic 'The' marks it as a word being talked about, not part of the sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: Grammar's name for 'the', and read literally, an item that is certain.

entries.clue: Pancake’s composition? (4-2)

blocks.note: pancake is a thick cake of cosmetic foundation used on stage
what something is composed of

annotation.surface: A cook asks what goes into a pancake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a batter recipe; pancake is also a type of stage cosmetic, which is the first definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pancake is an example of face cosmetics, and a thing's constitution is its composition.

entries.clue: Helping adult having a flutter? (8)

blocks.note: A = adult, as in film ratings
a flutter is a small bet, so having one is gambling

annotation.surface: A grown-up assisting with a little gamble.
annotation.walkthrough: A flutter is a small, casual bet in British English.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though usually said of helping someone do wrong.

entries.clue: Reprimanded Conservative gets protected (8)

blocks.note: C = Conservative
made safe or guaranteed, loosely protected

annotation.surface: A Tory who was told off is nonetheless shielded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reprimanded Conservative' reads as one phrase about a disciplined politician, but 'Reprimanded' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: formally rebuked.

entries.clue: Mark 50% of body passage (9)

blocks.note: the prefix meaning half
the large intestine, a passage in the body

annotation.surface: Half of a body passage bears a mark.
annotation.walkthrough: The body and punctuation share one word for different things, which is what makes the surface work.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is one punctuation mark.

entries.clue: Place item of golf equipment in chair (6)

blocks.note: to place = to set
the peg a golf ball sits on

annotation.surface: An instruction to put a golf peg down on an armchair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In chair' looks like a location; 'in' only joins, and 'chair' defines a seat for more than one.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose definition by kind: a sofa is a seat, stretched here to chair.

entries.clue: Fellows embracing male team coming first (6)

indicators.note: the fellows put their arms round the male

blocks.note: fellows = chaps
M = male

annotation.surface: Men hug a fellow team-mate after winning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Team coming first' is a descriptive definition; the answer is an informal short form of champions.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal clipping of champions, the side that finished first.

entries.clue: Blesses everyone in new show (7)

indicators.note: everyone goes in the rearranged show
new makes a new version of SHOW

blocks.note: SHOW rearranged
everyone = all

annotation.surface: A priest blesses the whole audience at a fresh production.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like the theatre, but only its four letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to make holy, as in 'hallowed be thy name'.

entries.clue: One making a hit in prison? (7)

blocks.note: someone who strikes hard or bangs things
a slang word for jail, from the slamming cell door

annotation.surface: A hitman ends up behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making a hit' suggests a contract killing, which fits the prison picture; it just means someone who strikes.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term for jail, and literally one who slams.

entries.clue: Gathers for prayers (8)

blocks.note: brings together
short set prayers in church services, stressed on the first syllable

annotation.surface: A congregation assembles in order to pray.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: the prayer is a COL-lect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for gathers, plus the liturgical name for short set prayers.

entries.clue: Acclaim King Charles starting change (6)

blocks.note: Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
to change a text

annotation.surface: Praise for the King as he begins a period of reform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starting' says the king comes first. The royal cipher on British postboxes uses the Latin initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: praise given for an achievement.

entries.clue: Nine roughly occupying accommodation – not strict (7)

indicators.note: roughly means not exactly, so NINE's letters come out in a rough order
the rearranged nine lives inside the accommodation

blocks.note: a rented property
NINE rearranged

annotation.surface: About nine people squat in a flat where the rules are lax.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nine roughly' reads as approximately nine; 'roughly' is the anagram signal. A let is British for a rented home.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tolerant and gentle, the opposite of strict.

entries.clue: Retire, relaxing with a thousand in ship (7)

indicators.note: relaxing loosens RETIRE so its letters can move

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the Roman numeral for a thousand, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone retires and unwinds on board with a thousand pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retire, relaxing' reads as a retirement cruise; the first word is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an ancient warship with three banks of oars.

entries.clue: Security device getting ordered outside – it creates obstruction (8)

indicators.note: the word for ordered goes outside the security device

blocks.note: past tense of bid, to order
a security device on a door

annotation.surface: A security gadget is ordered to be put outside, where it gets in the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an instruction in the story, but it is the old past tense of bid.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a naval or military cordon that obstructs traffic in and out.

entries.clue: No good having drink in small cup (6)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
G = good
a spirit

annotation.surface: It is no good drinking from a tiny cup.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is also slang for the head, but here it is the old sense of a small mug or a small measure of spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for a small mug or a small measure of drink.

entries.clue: Unhappy sound got bigger, as heard (5)

indicators.note: as heard means as it sounds when spoken

blocks.note: got bigger = grown; the spelling comes from the definition

annotation.surface: A complaining noise swelled until everyone could hear it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy sound' reads as a noise that got louder; 'sound' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A low moan of pain or dismay, a plain example of an unhappy sound.

entries.clue: Achieve something as cricketer and win lass’s heart (4,1,6,4)

blocks.note: a bowler's feat: six balls delivered with no runs scored off them
overwhelm a young woman with admiration

annotation.surface: A cricketer triumphs on the field and charms a girl too.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers six-ball overs; one conceding no runs is a maiden, a real achievement. 'Bowl over' also means overwhelm, and a maiden is a young woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricketing idiom for a scoreless over, and read literally, sweeping a young woman off her feet.

entries.clue: Guard second gate? (6)

blocks.note: S = second
a gate is a way in, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: Someone keeps watch at the second gate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guard' reads as a verb at a gate; it is the noun, the person on watch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a soldier posted to keep watch.

entries.clue: Position taken by remotest ancestors (6)

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

annotation.surface: A viewpoint held by one's most distant forebears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Position taken' reads as an opinion adopted; 'taken by' marks the letters lifted out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, covering both a physical posture and a view held in argument.
